clue.text: Understand downward measurement

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to work out or comprehend
second meaning: a unit of six feet used for sounding the depth of water

explanation.surface: Someone grasping how a depth is measured downwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one instruction; the two halves are separate meanings, a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to get to the bottom of something mentally, while the noun is the nautical unit of depth sounding.

clue.text: Seed in a load of old chestnuts?

parts.note: taken as written
corn means trite, hackneyed material, the stuff of old jokes

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a nut is found among a heap of chestnuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old chestnuts' look like nuts but mean stale, much-repeated jokes, and corn is a word for such stale stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the nut of the oak tree, the seed from which a new oak grows.

clue.text: Block after short journey creating minor diversion?

parts.note: a hop is a short trip, as in a quick flight
to scotch is to block or thwart, as a wedge stops a wheel

explanation.surface: A road closure after a short drive forces a small detour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diversion' reads as a detour but means amusement, and 'minor' points to a game for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a children's playground game, so it is literally a pastime for minors.

clue.text: Possible call from child, one kept under wraps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what a child calls its mother
second meaning: an embalmed body swathed in bandages

explanation.walkthrough: 'Under wraps' suggests secrecy, but it is literal here: an Egyptian body wrapped in linen.
explanation.definitionFit: A child calls out for its mother by this name, and the same word names an embalmed corpse wound in cloth.

clue.text: Enjoy what might add flavour

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to take great pleasure in
second meaning: a chutney or pickle served with food

explanation.surface: Savour whatever seasoning might liven up the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it is to savour with pleasure; as a noun it is a condiment such as pickle served alongside a meal.

clue.text: Method of torture alien and always criminal

parts.note: the rack was a frame for stretching victims
ET is the film alien, the extraterrestrial
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial forever subjected to torture, and also a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs a dishonest or illegal business, extortion and the like, so is a criminal.

clue.text: Gold daubed on bottom of white stick

indicators.note: daubed paint is smeared about carelessly, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder

indicators.note: in a down answer the bottom of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of the colour word

explanation.surface: Gold paint smeared on the end of a white walking stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like a noun, part of the white cane, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge is to become fixed or stuck in place, as a bone lodges in the throat.

clue.text: A new month occupying Chinese nation

indicators.note: something occupying a space sits within it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: Sino- is the prefix for Chinese
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
MAR is the short form of March

explanation.surface: A new calendar month taken over by China.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny independent republic enclosed by Italy, a sovereign nation in its own right.

clue.text: Gormless boss saving character from Athens

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a stud is a raised knob or boss on a surface
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A dim-witted manager rescues a figure from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' reads as a manager, but here it is a raised ornamental knob. Gormless is British for lacking sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Gormless is a British informal word for foolish and lacking sense, a straight synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Get a grip on composer, audibly

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so we want a word that is pronounced like the name

parts.note: George Frideric Handel, the baroque composer of Messiah

explanation.surface: Coming to terms with a composer, as heard on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle something is to manage or cope with it, which is getting a grip on it figuratively and literally.

clue.text: Unit also crossing river, heading for Paris

indicators.note: one word crossing another is pictured with the second running through the middle of the first

parts.note: a synonym meaning as well
R is the standard abbreviation for river

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, so only the initial is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of the French capital's name

explanation.surface: A military unit wading across a river on its way to the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The river letter sits inside the word for 'also', and the Paris initial is tacked on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a body of soldiers, a recognised subdivision of a cavalry or artillery regiment.

clue.text: Dud and I came to tour old country

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all round it, so these letters surround another piece
a dud is something faulty, so the letters that follow are taken as broken and rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken letter by letter
O is a common abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A failure and the speaker arrived to travel round some historic land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dud' reads as a noun for a failure, but it signals the anagram; 'old' gives the single O that the shuffled letters wrap round. 'Old country' looks like the definition but 'old' is needed for wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedonia is a historic Balkan region and kingdom, the name used by the modern republic now called North Macedonia.

clue.text: Cooking vessel disgusting, so in a tizzy

parts.note: a pan is a pot for cooking
informal word for nasty or gross

explanation.surface: A filthy saucepan sends the cook into a flap.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a tizzy means being in a state of nervous agitation, which is what a panicky person is.

clue.text: Gem finally pocketed by dodgy dealer — this one?

indicators.note: something pocketed is tucked inside, so one piece goes within the other
dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are not to be trusted in their given order

parts.note: the anagram fodder

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the closing letter of this word

explanation.surface: A shifty trader slips a jewel into his pocket, and the question asks which stone it was.
explanation.walkthrough: The M from the end of 'Gem' goes after the first letter of the rearranged DEALER. 'This one?' makes the whole clue point back at the gem as a semi-all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: An emerald is a green precious stone, a variety of beryl, so it is one example of a gem.

clue.text: Dubious article between furniture items, face to face

indicators.note: something between two others is enclosed by them, one on each side
for two items to face each other the first must be turned round to look back at the second

parts.note: the first piece of furniture, a bed, turned round
the indefinite article
the second piece of furniture, a table

explanation.surface: A questionable choice of where to place a grammatical word among the furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Furniture items' supplies two words, a bed and a table, with the article between them; the bed is turned so the two face each other across it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something debatable is open to question or argument, which is what dubious means here.

clue.text: Restaurant put some orchestral players on lake

parts.note: the brass section of an orchestra
Lake Erie, one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A dining place has booked part of an orchestra to play by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, putting one piece on another stacks it above, so it comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French-style eatery, a type of restaurant.

clue.text: State in existence, working hard

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: being is the state of existing
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A country still in being, toiling away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a nation but is the verb meaning declare.
explanation.definitionFit: Beavering away means working diligently, like a beaver busily building its dam.

clue.text: Adjoining rooms adorable, by the sound of it

indicators.note: we are told to go by what is heard rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: adorable means cute or charming; the word for that is pronounced the same as the answer

explanation.surface: An estate agent praising a lovely set of connected rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A suite is a set of connected rooms, as in a hotel, so the rooms adjoin one another.

clue.text: Model in a closet in various pieces

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so the letters are formed into something new

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A fashion model hiding in a cupboard, in bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a person, but it is a verb telling us to reshape the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sectional furniture comes in separate units that fit together, so it is made in several parts.

clue.text: Straight path's ending below

parts.note: neat as in undiluted, a straight drink

indicators.note: a word's ending here is just its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of the word path

explanation.surface: A direct path winds down at its end to lower ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Neat and straight both describe spirits served without water.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Neath is a poetic shortening of beneath, meaning under or below.

clue.text: Detect water as liquid or vapour, by deduction?

parts.note: liquid or vapour are the forms that are not the solid one
ice is water in its solid form

explanation.surface: A scientist working out the state of some water by reasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: If water is liquid or vapour, then by deduction it is not ice: a playful logic puzzle, flagged by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice is to observe or become aware of something, which is what detecting means.

clue.text: Foolish Icarus, too shocking

indicators.note: foolish suggests letters behaving senselessly, so they are muddled up

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Icarus, who flew too near the sun, was reckless and appalling as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrocious means appallingly bad or wicked, a close synonym of shocking.

clue.text: Redevelopment of Dorset dealt with

indicators.note: redeveloping a site rebuilds it in a new layout, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, an English county

explanation.surface: Planning for rebuilding in an English county has been handled.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorted is informal British for settled or taken care of, matching dealt with.

clue.text: Assessment devoured, having the will

parts.note: a test is an assessment
past tense of eat

explanation.surface: Someone's exam paper was eaten, though they were determined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having the will' sounds like determination, but it means having made a legal will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testate person died leaving a valid legal will, as opposed to intestate.

clue.text: Killer doctor after mix of blood types?

parts.note: the ABO system: A, B and O are the main blood groups
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A murderous physician who tampered with patients' blood transfusions.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark acknowledges the blood groups are lifted in a loose bundle, A, B and O, rather than one word.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomic bomb is a weapon of mass destruction, deadly on a vast scale, so it is a killer.

clue.text: Cheerful sculptor?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsically: one who chips away at stone

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second meaning as a playful one: a sculptor is literally someone who chips.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is informal for bright and in good spirits; as a noun it fancifully names one who carves by chipping.

clue.text: Tweet deserving contempt, did you say?

indicators.note: asking what was said points to how a word is pronounced

parts.note: cheap as in tawdry and contemptible

explanation.surface: Someone queries a social-media post that seems worthy of scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweet' suggests a social-media post, but it is the noise a small bird makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheep is the short high chirp of a young bird, the same sound as a tweet.

clue.text: Smooth journalists

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the news reporters collectively

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description of slick reporters, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To press clothes is to iron them smooth, and the press is the collective name for newspapers and reporters.

clue.text: Hurtful, shade reflective having broken heart

indicators.note: the other word is broken open and this one sits in the gap

parts.note: the heart of something is its core

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the word is turned round

parts.note: a visor is an eyeshade

explanation.surface: Someone sad and thoughtful, nursing a broken heart, says cutting things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade' tempts a colour, but it is an eyeshade, turned round and placed inside the word for heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrosive remarks eat away at someone like acid, so the word figuratively means harmful or wounding.

clue.text: Relative in Greece injured back

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in the opposite direction
in tells us the letters are found inside the following words

parts.note: the letters running across the end of the country name and start of the next word

explanation.surface: A family member was hurt while holidaying in Greece and is recovering.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a family member, the daughter of one's brother or sister.

clue.text: Label covering each black container full of holes

indicators.note: a covering wraps round what it covers, so the first word goes outside the rest

parts.note: a tag is a label
EA is the standard abbreviation for each
B for black, as in pencil grades

explanation.surface: Instructions for labelling every dark sieve-like box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Container full of holes' sounds like a useless one, but a porous bag holding leaves is exactly what is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea bag is a small porous paper sachet holding tea leaves, perforated so water can pass through.

clue.text: Perfect Europeans

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to refine or improve
second meaning: of Poland, as in the people of that nation

explanation.walkthrough: The capital letter is hidden by sitting at the start of the clue: one meaning is lower-case, the other the nationality from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish is to refine work to a finished state; capitalised, it names the people of Poland collectively.
